arxiv-2109-10919.title: An Exploration of Learnt Representations of W Jets
arxiv-2109-10919.creator: Jack H. Collins
arxiv-2109-10919.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jack H. Collins. I present a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) trained on collider physics data (specifically boosted W W jets), with reconstruction error given by an approximation to the Earth Movers Distance (EMD) between input and output jets. This VAE learns a concrete representation of the data manifold, with semantically meaningful and interpretable latent space directions which are hierarchically organized in terms of their relation to physical EMD scales in the underlying physical generative process.

arxiv-2212-05701.title: Collective Vector Clocks: Low-Overhead Transparent Checkpointing for MPI
arxiv-2212-05701.creator: Yao Xu, Gene Cooperman
arxiv-2212-05701.description: Abstract Taking snapshots of the state of a distributed computation is useful for off-line analysis of the computational state, for later restarting from the saved snapshot, for cloning a copy of the computation, and for migration to a new cluster.

arxiv-2409-08955.title: High-Temperature Non-Equilibrium Atom-Diatom Collisional Energy Transfer
arxiv-2409-08955.creator: Xiaorui Zhao, Xuefei Xu, Haitao Xu
arxiv-2409-08955.description: Abstract The change of the vibrational energy within a molecule after collisions with another molecule plays an essential role in the evolution of molecular internal energy distributions, which is also the limiting process in the relaxation of the gas towards equilibrium.

arxiv-2506-00489.title: A phylogeny of biological patterns formed by nonlocal advection
arxiv-2506-00489.creator: Valeria Giunta, Thomas Hillen, Mark A Lewis, Jonathan R Potts
arxiv-2506-00489.description: Abstract From tumour invasion to cell sorting and animal territoriality, many biological systems rely on nonlocal interactions that drive complex spatial organisation. Partial differential equations (PDEs) with nonlocal advection are increasingly recognised as powerful tools for capturing such phenomena. However, most research has focused on one-dimensional domains, leaving their two-dimensional behaviour largely unexplored.

britannica-1911-mountstephen-george-step.title: Mountstephen, George Stephen, Baron (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-mountstephen-george-step.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-mountstephen-george-step.description: Article 'Mountstephen, George Stephen, Baron' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Canadian financier, was born on the 5th of June 1829 at Dufftown, Banffshire, Scotland, the son of William Stephen and Elspeth Smith. He was educated at the parish school, after which he was for a time a herd boy. In 1850 he went to Canada and soon became a prominent business man in Montreal.

britannica-1911-twining-thomas.title: Twining, Thomas (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-twining-thomas.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-twining-thomas.description: Article 'Twining, Thomas' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 27), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. was born at Twickenham on the 8th of January 1734–1735. The son of Daniel Twining, tea merchant of London, he was originally intended for a commercial life, but his distaste for it and his fondness for study decided his father to send him to the university.

pmc-11410806.title: Deep generative models of protein structure uncover distant relationships across a continuous fold space
pmc-11410806.creator: Eli J. Draizen, Stella Veretnik, Cameron Mura, Philip E. Bourne
pmc-11410806.description: Our views of fold space implicitly rest upon many assumptions that impact how we analyze, interpret and understand protein structure, function and evolution. For instance, is there an optimal granularity in viewing protein structural similarities (e.g., architecture, topology or some other level)? Similarly, the discrete/continuous dichotomy of fold space is central, but remains unresolved.

pmc-11590856.title: Effectiveness of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists for reduction of body mass index and blood glucose control in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus and obesity: A retrospective cohort study and difference-in-difference analysis
pmc-11590856.creator: Sukanya Siriyotha, Thunyarat Anothaisintawee, Panu Looareesuwan, Hataikarn Nimitphong, Gareth J McKay, John Attia, Ammarin Thakkinstian
pmc-11590856.description: AbstractObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) in reducing body mass index (BMI) and blood glucose levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) using the difference-in-differences (DID) technique.Research design and methodsThis retrospective cohort study included patients with T2DM, receiving GLP1-RA or other second-line antidiabetic treatments between 2010 and 2023.

pmc-11632978.title: PPP1R14B as a potential biomarker for the identification of diagnosis and prognosis affecting tumor immunity, proliferation and migration in prostate cancer
pmc-11632978.creator: Yizhong Bao, Yixiu Ni, Aokang Zhang, Jun Chen
pmc-11632978.description: Prostate cancer (PCa) is a malignancy that affects men and is characterized by metastasis and high rates of morbidity. The objective of this study was to explore novel PCa biomarker with potential diagnostic and therapeutic value and relationships between it and tumor immunity and development.

pmc-12574268.title: Machine learning in biological research: key algorithms, applications, and future directions
pmc-12574268.creator: Md Nafis Ul Alam, Kiran Basava, Ani Chitransh, H. M. Abdul Fattah, Hector D. Garcia-Verdugo, Shih-Hsuan Lo, Tanisha Lohchab, Kristen M. Martinet, Cristian Román-Palacios, Jhan Carlos Salazar, Danielle Van Boxel
pmc-12574268.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Machine learning is a robust framework to analyze questions using complex data in a variety of fields. We present definitions and recent applications of four key machine learning methods and discuss their advantages and challenges in biological research. Through a set of systematically selected case studies, we highlight how machine learning models have been used in a range of applications, including phylogenomics, disease prediction, and host taxonomy prediction.

pmc-12609034.title: Jerked Beef: Chemical Composition and Desalting Techniques
pmc-12609034.creator: Maria do Desterro Pereira Ferreira Ibiapina, Maria Eduarda Corino de Melo, Márcio Antônio Mendonça, Frederico Lopes da Silva, Myller de Sousa Tonhá, Raquel Braz Assunção Botelho
pmc-12609034.description: The present study aims to compare the chemical composition of samples of jerked beef commercialized in Brasilia, Brazil, subjected to diverse desalting techniques (room temperature, refrigerated, and heat desalting). This experimental study was divided into five steps: determination of desalting techniques, chemical composition, determination of titratable acidity and pH, sodium analysis of the samples, and statistical analysis.

pmc-12663306.title: An efficient deep learning-based morphology aware hierarchical mixture of features for tuberculosis screening using segmentation of chest X-ray images
pmc-12663306.creator: Mashael Maashi, Huda Eltayeb, Mashael M. Asiri, Rakan Alanazi, Abdulmohsen Saud Albesher, Eman M. Alanazi, Rowida Mohammed Alharbi, Monir Abdullah
pmc-12663306.description: Tuberculosis (TB) is a chronic lung disorder caused by bacterial infection and is a major cause of death. Lung cancer also has a significant impact, and existing solutions concentrate on initial screening, which mainly results in better outcomes at a comparatively lower cost.

pmc-13049077.title: Celastrol attenuates Th1- and Th2-driven skin inflammation in 2D and 3D in vitro models
pmc-13049077.creator: Kirsten Reddersen, Bianka Morgner, Oliver Werz, Stefan Lorkowski, Dagmar Fischer, Jörg Tittelbach, Cornelia Wiegand
pmc-13049077.description: Celastrol, a bioactive compound from Tripterygium wilfordii Hook F, has been reported to exert potent anti-inflammatory effects through multiple signaling pathways. While its activity has been studied in various cell types and disease models, its effects in atopic dermatitis (AD) is limited to a few studies in mouse models and remains largely unexplored in in vitro cell models.

pmc-13100240.title: Integrated transcriptomics and single-cell analysis identify ITGAX⁺ macrophages as key immunosuppressive factors in the prostate cancer tumor microenvironment
pmc-13100240.creator: Yi Shao, Shengju Song, Wei Wang, Liwei Liu, Jing Tian, Peng Zhang, Zhiqun Shang
pmc-13100240.description: BackgroundProstate cancer (PCa) is a leading cause of cancer-related death in men worldwide. The tumor microenvironment (TME), particularly its immune and stromal components, has a critical influence on PCa progression and patient outcomes. Identifying novel TME-associated biomarkers is important for better understanding PCa progression and may inform future diagnostic or therapeutic strategies.

pmc-13613982.title: Breaking steric hindrance restriction: compressed metal bonds realizing deep-level orbital delocalization
pmc-13613982.creator: Hanghao Ying, Liuxin Xu, Xia Zhong, Yi Liu, Xiaodong Zhang, Yi Xie
pmc-13613982.description: The introduction of large functional groups is a well-established strategy to enhance the stability and value of chemicals. However, accompanying steric hindrance effects can significantly impede the reaction progress, presenting a critical dilemma in synthetic design. Herein, a vacancy-constrained strategy was proposed for breaking steric hindrance restriction by realizing the deep-level delocalization of a catalyst with compressed metal bonds.

uslaw-usc-t10-s1079a.title: 10 U.S.C. § 1079a — TRICARE program: treatment of refunds and other amounts collected
uslaw-usc-t10-s1079a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s1079a.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part II (Personnel); Chapter 55 (Medical And Dental Care). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. All refunds and other amounts collected in the administration of the TRICARE program shall be credited to the appropriation available for that program for the fiscal year in which the refund or amount is collected.

uslaw-usc-t42-s11320.title: 42 U.S.C. § 11320 — Encouragement of State involvement
uslaw-usc-t42-s11320.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s11320.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 119 (Homeless Assistance); Subchapter II (United States Interagency Council On Homelessness). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) State contact persons Each State shall designate an individual to serve as a State contact person for the purpose of receiving and disseminating information and communications received from the Council, including the bimonthly bulletin.
